bib.title: MLE-bench: Evaluating Machine Learning Agents on Machine Learning Engineering

read.skipped: Table 8 per-competition rows and the A.8 obfuscated description text were skimmed; Fig 3/4/5/9 curves are images

question: How well can AI agents perform end-to-end machine learning engineering, measured against human Kaggle results?
contributions: Large-scale evaluations of frontier models and agent scaffolds
Experiments on contamination and plagiarism/cheating detection

method.summary: 75 Kaggle competitions are ported to an offline environment with local grading and private-leaderboard medal thresholds. Agents (AIDE, MLAB, OpenHands) with several LLMs get 24 hours, one A10 GPU and a validation server, and are scored by the share of attempts earning any medal.

datasets.name: MLE-bench
datasets.size: 75 competitions (22 Low, 38 Medium, 15 High complexity) plus 7 development competitions; selected from 5673 Kaggle competitions, 586 manually screened
datasets.split: test set is 10% of original train unless stated, else original test; Low split recommended if resources are short
datasets.source: Kaggle (Meta Kaggle list, accessed May 15 2024); private leaderboard snapshots May-August 2024
datasets.preprocessing: descriptions scraped from Overview and Data tabs; grading code reimplemented; submissions simplified to CSV; new splits checked via sample submission scoring similarly

other.use: log analysis tool (A.3); Sec 2.3.1 says GPT-4o

inference.samples: 3 seeds per competition (mean and standard error); o1-preview AIDE 16 seeds, GPT-4o AIDE 36 seeds; obfuscation run 10 seeds; pass@k uses n seeds
inference.prompting: common overall instruction prompt (Fig 8) plus time/steps remaining each turn

parameters.AIDE: agent.steps 2000 (main text: 500 nodes max; 100h run 5000 nodes), max_debug_depth 20, debug_prob 1, time_limit 86400, exec.timeout 32400, feedback model gpt-4o-2024-08-06

other.hardware: Azure Standard_NV36ads_A10_v5: 36 vCPUs, 440GB RAM, 4095 GiB SSD, one 24GB A10 GPU; Ubuntu 20.04 Docker, sysbox
other.validation: local server, no score, unlimited calls
other.rules: no hand-labelling, no viewing online solutions; Dolos plagiarism threshold 60%, k=23, top 50 notebooks
other.note: AIDE step cap is 2000 in Table 7 but text says 500 nodes

metrics.name: Any medal
metrics.definition: percentage of attempts awarded any medal (bronze or above) relative to private leaderboard, thresholds from Table 1 applied to all competitions

metrics.name: Raw score / above median / valid submission
metrics.definition: per-competition raw metric; share above median; share with valid submission

baselines: MLAB and OpenHands scaffolds vs AIDE
eval.protocol: mean ± one standard error of the mean over seeds; scaffold modifications listed in A.6

availability.data: rebuilt from Kaggle by provided code

prompts.text: You are participating in *MLE-bench*, an offline version of Kaggle competitions adapted to test the coding ability of agents like yourself. You will be given a machine learning task. You must solve the task by training a model and running the model on the test set to produce a submission file. You may not hand-label the data to produce a submission file. (followed by benchmark instructions: description at /home/data/description.md, data in /home/data/, submission at /home/submission/submission.csv, validation server at http://localhost:5000/validate, no viewing others' solutions)

limits: Contamination: models may have trained on Kaggle material; Titanic rows reproduced by GPT-4 base; experiments only test GPT-4o and cannot rule out subtle high-level-strategy leakage
Tasks have clear statements, clean data and clear metrics; do not cover open-ended AI R&D
New splits and reimplemented grading may differ from human leaderboards; older competitions may be easier with today's tools
Resource intensive: 1800 GPU hours per run and large token use; 3 seeds only for most settings
Gemini-1.5-Pro could not be evaluated (recitation blocks)
Models struggle on competitions after 2022, and agents misjudge compute/time and fail to validate submissions
AIDE best-attempt selection is imperfect, so medals sometimes fall over time
Sample sizes: complexity-subset results have wide standard errors; no decoding parameters reported
